name: The creek basin at the rising tide
subject: geography
brief: A bunded creek basin near Gosaba in the Sundarbans held 4,200 cubic metres at slack low water. During the next 6 hours of rising tide the sluice register logs 650 cubic metres an hour coming in through the lifted shutter. The off-take register for the irrigation channels shows 125 in each entry, and in small print the column is headed cubic metres per half-hour. How many cubic metres will the basin hold at the end of the 6 hours? You are the recorder, and the period is nearly over.

quantities.name: Cubic metres of water in the basin
Cubic metres through the sluice an hour
Cubic metres into the irrigation channels an hour
Height of the ring bund above datum in metres

note: Sundarbans tidal hydrology for Class XI geography; Gosaba is a real island in the delta. Worked answer: the off-take of 125 cubic metres per half-hour is 125 x 2 = 250 cubic metres an hour. The basin gains (650 - 250) = 400 cubic metres an hour, over 6 hours that is 400 x 6 = 2,400, and the basin ends at 4,200 + 2,400 = 6,600 cubic metres. The scale fault is the mixed units: reading 125 as an hourly figure would give (650 - 125) x 6 = 3,150 more and a final 7,350 cubic metres, which is wrong by 750.
